Biodegradable plastic bag.why: The Green Guides say that an unqualified biodegradable claim for items entering the solid waste stream is deceptive if the items do not completely decompose within one year after customary disposal. Plastic bags are typically disposed of in landfills, incinerators, or recycling facilities, where they will not degrade within one year.
Biodegradable plastic bag.quote: It is deceptive to make an unqualified degradable claim for items entering the solid waste stream if the items do not completely decompose within one year after customary disposal.

Carbon neutral shipping.why: The Green Guides state that sellers should use competent and reliable methods to quantify emission reductions and ensure they do not sell the same reduction more than once. The claim also needs qualification if the emission reductions will not occur for two years or longer.
Carbon neutral shipping.quote: Given the complexities of carbon offsets, sellers should employ competent and reliable scientific and accounting methods to properly quantify claimed emission reductions and to ensure that they do not sell the same reduction more than one time.

Made with ocean plastic.why: The Green Guides do not name or clearly describe claims about 'ocean plastic' or materials sourced from the ocean.

100% recyclable packaging.why: The Green Guides say that an unqualified recyclable claim is deceptive if recycling facilities are not available to a substantial majority (at least 60%) of consumers where the item is sold. This claim does not specify the availability of facilities.
100% recyclable packaging.quote: Marketers should clearly and prominently qualify recyclable claims to the extent necessary to avoid deception about the availability of recycling programs and collection sites to consumers.
